title: Some US Scientists Move Abroad as Research Funding Shrinks
summaryZh: 美國研究經費遭削減，部分科學家轉往芬蘭、澳洲等國工作。
summaryHi: शोध के पैसे में कटौती से कुछ अमेरिकी वैज्ञानिक दूसरे देशों में जा रहे हैं।
summaryEs: Los recortes en la financiación de la investigación llevan a algunos científicos de EE. UU. a irse al extranjero.

summaryEn: Because of cuts and delays in government research money, some American scientists are moving to jobs in other countries.
paragraphs: A steady stream of American researchers is relocating overseas, frustrated by cuts, freezes and long delays in federal science funding, according to an Associated Press report published on Monday.

Since the start of President Trump's second term, up to $174 billion in federal grants has been cut or frozen, according to two organisations that monitor the money. Climate research has been among the hardest-hit areas, and some scientists say they have also faced political pressure over what they study.

Halley Froehlich, a marine scientist who examines how seafood responds to climate change, has moved from the University of California, Santa Barbara, to the University of Helsinki, attracted by a Finnish scheme that will give her about $3 million over five years. A married couple left UC Davis for Monash University in Australia after funding stalled, and Nobel chemistry laureate Omar Yaghi has gone to lead an AI lab in China.

Canada, France, Belgium and Finland are among the countries actively recruiting US-based scientists with promises of stable funding and academic freedom. Physics PhD graduates left the US in 2025 at the highest rate in three decades.

The White House insists it is eliminating waste and remains committed to 'real science'. Not every researcher is leaving, but leading universities admitted 15 percent fewer doctoral students this autumn, and experts fear the effects could be felt for a decade or longer.
Some scientists in the United States are leaving the country. They are moving to other countries to do their work.

Why? Many scientists get money for their research from the US government. But in the last two years, the government has cut or stopped a lot of this money. Some scientists waited a long time for money, and some lost it.
Halley Froehlich studies fish and the changing climate. She worked at a university in California. Now she works in Finland. Finland is giving her about 3 million dollars for five years.
A married couple from a university in California moved to Australia. A famous chemist who won a Nobel Prize moved to China.
Other countries, like Canada and France, want these scientists. The White House says it still pays for good science. But experts worry that the US may lose many young scientists.

A growing number of American scientists are leaving the United States to work abroad, according to a report by the Associated Press. Many say cuts and long delays in government research money have made their work too difficult.

Since President Trump began his second term, the government has cut or frozen up to $174 billion in research grants, according to two groups that track the money. Climate research has been hit especially hard.

Halley Froehlich, who studies how seafood is affected by climate change, left the University of California, Santa Barbara, for the University of Helsinki in Finland. A Finnish program is giving her about $3 million over five years. Others have moved to Britain and Australia, and Nobel Prize winner Omar Yaghi now runs a lab in China.
Countries such as Canada, France, Belgium and Finland have special programs to attract US researchers, promising stable money and freedom to choose their research.

A White House spokesperson said the government is ending waste and still supports real science. However, many universities are taking fewer PhD students, and experts warn the damage could last ten years or more.
A steady stream of American researchers is relocating overseas, frustrated by cuts, freezes and long delays in federal science funding, according to an Associated Press report published on Monday.

Since the start of President Trump's second term, up to $174 billion in federal grants has been cut or frozen, according to two organisations that monitor the money. Climate research has been among the hardest-hit areas, and some scientists say they have also faced political pressure over what they study.

Halley Froehlich, a marine scientist who examines how seafood responds to climate change, has moved from the University of California, Santa Barbara, to the University of Helsinki, attracted by a Finnish scheme that will give her about $3 million over five years. A married couple left UC Davis for Monash University in Australia after funding stalled, and Nobel chemistry laureate Omar Yaghi has gone to lead an AI lab in China.

Canada, France, Belgium and Finland are among the countries actively recruiting US-based scientists with promises of stable funding and academic freedom. Physics PhD graduates left the US in 2025 at the highest rate in three decades.

The White House insists it is eliminating waste and remains committed to 'real science'. Not every researcher is leaving, but leading universities admitted 15 percent fewer doctoral students this autumn, and experts fear the effects could be felt for a decade or longer.

A trickle of American scientists heading abroad is turning into a noticeable outflow, as researchers weary of slashed budgets, frozen grants and political interference seek more stable footing elsewhere, the Associated Press reported on Monday.

Watchdog groups estimate that as much as $174 billion in federal grants has been cancelled or suspended since President Trump returned to office. Climate science has borne the brunt, and some researchers say they were instructed to scrub references to climate change and diversity from official websites.

Among the departures is marine scientist Halley Froehlich, whose family has lived in the US since the 1700s; she has taken up a post at the University of Helsinki, lured by roughly $3 million in guaranteed funding over five years. Others have decamped to Britain and Australia, while Nobel laureate Omar Yaghi now heads an AI laboratory at Tsinghua University in Beijing.

Canada, France, Belgium and Finland have all trumpeted their success in poaching US-based talent, and the American Institute of Physics found that new physics PhDs left the country in 2025 at the fastest rate in 30 years.

The White House maintains that it is merely rooting out waste. Yet with major universities admitting 15 percent fewer doctoral candidates this year, experts warn that the erosion of training and mentorship could hamper American science for a generation.

An increasing number of scientists are leaving the United States to continue their careers abroad, according to a recent Associated Press report. The trend raises important questions about how government funding decisions influence a country's ability to retain talented researchers.

Since the current administration took office, up to $174 billion in federal research grants has reportedly been cut or frozen. Many scientists describe long delays and growing uncertainty, while some claim that political considerations now affect which projects receive support. Climate research appears to have been particularly affected.

Several countries have responded by actively recruiting American researchers. Finland, for example, is providing marine scientist Halley Froehlich with approximately $3 million over five years, and Canada, France and Belgium have launched similar programmes that promise stable funding and academic freedom.

Supporters of the government's approach argue that it is simply eliminating wasteful spending, and the White House maintains that it remains committed to genuine science. Critics, however, point out that leading universities accepted 15 percent fewer doctoral students this year.

Experts warn that the consequences may be long-lasting. If fewer young people are trained and fewer experienced scientists remain to mentor them, the country's research capacity could decline for a decade or more.

reported.ex: The theft was reported to the police.

reportedly.ja: 伝えられるところでは
reportedly.en: according to what people say or report
reportedly.ex: The singer has reportedly cancelled her tour.

research.ex: Research shows that exercise helps sleep.

researcher.en: a person who studies something in detail
researcher.ex: The researcher spent years studying ocean plants.

responded.ex: He responded to my message quickly.

responds.ex: The plant responds quickly to more sunlight.

retain.ex: The firm wants to retain its best workers.

example.en: The company raised pay to retain its best staff.
example.zh: 公司加薪以留住最好的員工。

note.usage: 常見 retain staff/talent/control；名詞 retention；比 keep 正式。

noteEn.meaning: to keep someone or something, and not lose them.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'retain staff/talent'; more formal than 'keep'; noun: retention.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी ने अच्छे कर्मचारियों को रोकने के लिए वेतन बढ़ाया।
noteHi.usage: retain staff/talent आम हैं; keep से औपचारिक।

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa subió los sueldos para retener a su mejor personal.
noteEs.usage: Se usa retain staff/talent; más formal que keep.

noteJa.exampleTr: 会社は優秀な社員を引き留めるため給料を上げた。
noteJa.usage: retain staff/talent の形が多い。keep より硬い。

noteKo.exampleTr: 회사는 우수 직원을 붙잡기 위해 임금을 올렸다.

returned.en: went back to an earlier state
returned.ex: Life returned to normal after the storm.

rooting.en: finding and removing something bad (rooting out)
rooting.ex: The new boss is rooting out waste in the office.

runs.ex: Her family runs a small hotel.

s.ex: The club has a team for under-12s.

santa.en: "Saint" in Spanish names like Santa Ana

say.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

says.ex: Experts say the plan will work.

scheme.ex: The bike scheme is popular in Dublin.

science.ex: She has loved science since she was a child.

scientists.ex: Scientists are studying the new virus.

scrub.ex: They had to scrub the old data from the system.

seafood.en: fish and shellfish eaten as food
seafood.ex: The town is famous for its fresh seafood.

seek.ex: The agency is seeking a new partner.

similar.ex: My bag is similar to yours.

simply.ex: Some crops simply cannot grow here.

slashed.ex: The shop slashed prices to attract more customers.

some.ex: Some fifty people came to the meeting.

special.ex: The area has a special feeling.

spokesperson.en: a person who speaks for a group
spokesperson.ex: A spokesperson for the police gave a statement.

stable.ex: A stable job helps people plan their future.

states.ex: EU member states agreed the plan.

steady.ex: There has been a steady rise in house prices.

stopped.ex: The rain stopped in the afternoon.

stream.en: a moving flow of air or water

studies.ex: She studies how birds find their way home.

study.ex: A new study shows the risks.

success.ex: The concert was a great success.

support.ja: 支援（support staff：支援スタッフ）

supporters.en: people who agree with and help an idea
supporters.ex: Supporters of the new park held a meeting.

supports.ex: The town offers supports for new businesses.

suspended.en: stopped for a period of time
suspended.ex: Train services were suspended during the storm.

example.en: The union suspended the strike to allow more talks.
example.zh: 工會暫停了罷工，好讓雙方有更多時間談判。

note.meaning: 暫時停止某項行動或服務，之後可能恢復。
note.usage: 常用被動 be suspended；注意與 cancel（取消）不同，suspend 表示「暫停」而非永久終止。

noteHi.exampleTr: यूनियन ने और बातचीत के लिए हड़ताल स्थगित कर दी।
noteHi.meaning: किसी काम या सेवा को कुछ समय के लिए रोकना, जो बाद में फिर शुरू हो सकता है।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर passive में: be suspended; cancel (रद्द करना) से अलग, इसका अर्थ अस्थायी रोक है।

noteEs.exampleTr: El sindicato suspendió la huelga para permitir más conversaciones.
noteEs.meaning: detener algo temporalmente, con la posibilidad de reanudarlo después.
noteEs.usage: Se usa mucho en pasiva (be suspended); no es lo mismo que cancel, que es definitivo.

noteJa.exampleTr: 組合はさらなる協議のためにストライキを一時中止した。
noteJa.meaning: 行動やサービスを一時的に止めること。後で再開される可能性がある。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be suspended がよく使われる。cancel（中止）とは違い、一時的な停止を表す。

noteKo.exampleTr: 노조는 추가 협상을 위해 파업을 중단했다.
noteKo.meaning: 어떤 행동이나 서비스를 일시적으로 멈추는 것으로, 나중에 다시 시작될 수 있다.
noteKo.usage: 수동태 be suspended로 자주 쓰인다. cancel(취소)과 달리 일시적인 중단을 뜻한다.

noteEn.meaning: to stop something for a time, so it may start again later.
noteEn.usage: Often passive: "be suspended". It is not the same as "cancel", which is final.

taking.ex: Many students are taking part in the race.

talent.en: a natural ability to do something well
talent.ex: He has a talent for drawing.

talented.ex: The school attracts talented students from abroad.

term.en: a word or phrase with a special meaning
term.ex: 'Fast fashion' is a common term today.

these.en: the ones here or just mentioned

time.ex: For the first time, dentists will join.

too.ex: The coffee is too hot to drink.

took.en: used in 'took part' meaning joined in
took.ex: Everyone took part in the game.

track.ex: The storm's track is hard to predict.

trained.en: taught the skills for a job
trained.ex: She trained as a nurse in London.

training.ex: New staff get two weeks of training.

trend.en: a general change or popular fashion
trend.ex: Working from home is a growing trend.

trickle.ex: A trickle of visitors came back after the storm.

trump.en: Donald Trump, President of the United States

trumpeted.ex: The company trumpeted its record sales.

turning.en: going to for help or a solution
turning.ex: More people are turning to online shopping.

uncertainty.en: a situation in which something is not known
uncertainty.ex: There is uncertainty about the weather.

example.en: There is growing uncertainty about the economy.
example.zh: 外界對經濟的不確定感日增。

note.usage: 常見 uncertainty about/over sth；economic/political uncertainty。

noteEn.meaning: a situation in which things are not known or clear.

noteHi.exampleTr: अर्थव्यवस्था को लेकर अनिश्चितता बढ़ रही है।
noteHi.meaning: अनिश्चितता; साफ़ न होने की स्थिति।
noteHi.usage: uncertainty about sth; economic uncertainty आम हैं।

noteEs.exampleTr: Crece la incertidumbre sobre la economía.

noteJa.exampleTr: 経済をめぐる不確実性が高まっている。
noteJa.meaning: 不確実性；先が見えないこと。

united.zh: 美國（United States 的一部分）
united.en: part of the name United States; joined together
united.ex: The United States has fifty states.

university.ex: She wants to study law at university.

us-based.en: working or located in the US
us-based.ex: She joined a US-based charity last year.

waited.ex: They waited two hours for the bus.

warn.en: to say something bad may happen

waste.en: things thrown away because no longer needed
waste.ex: Put food waste in the brown bin.

wasteful.ex: Leaving lights on all night is wasteful.

watchdog.en: a group that checks others follow rules
watchdog.ex: The consumer watchdog fined the bank.

weary.ex: Weary of delays, they found new jobs abroad.

websites.en: pages or places on the internet
websites.ex: Many websites ask you to accept cookies.

were.ex: The shops were closed on Sunday.

will.en: used to talk about the future
will.ex: The new bridge will open next year.

winner.ex: The prize winner gave a short speech.

won.ex: Our team won the cup last year.

work.ex: Robots can do some hard work.

worked.ex: They worked hard on the project.

works.ex: My father works in a bank.

yet.ex: I haven't finished my homework yet.
yet.zh: 還（沒）；然而；has yet to：尚未

young.ex: Young people often use social media.
